scope: Corollary 8.2 (Ordering-CSP consequence) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ≥ 2 and ∅ ̸= Π ⊊ Sk, and put ρΠ = |Π|/k!. For every fixed 0 < ε < (1 − ρΠ)/2, it is NP-hard to distinguish finite weighted Π-ordering-CSP instances I satisfying OPTΠ(I) ≥ 1 − ε from those satisfying OPTΠ(I) ≤ ρΠ + ε. Consequently, approximation at every fixed ratio r ∈ (ρΠ, 1] is NP-hard. Together with the random- ordering guarantee, this gives the optimal threshold ρΠ.
